title: Higher-Order Observables: mergeMap, concatMap, switchMap, exhaustMap

questions.prompt: A new outer value arrives while the previous inner Observable is still running. Which operator CANCELS the previous inner and switches to the new one?

options.text: switchMap
concatMap
mergeMap
exhaustMap

questions.explanation: switchMap unsubscribes from the in-flight inner and subscribes to the newest one, so only the latest inner survives.

questions.prompt: Which operator is the right default for search-as-you-type, and why?

options.text: switchMap — it cancels stale requests so old responses can't overwrite fresh ones
mergeMap — it runs all requests in parallel for speed
concatMap — it guarantees results arrive in typing order
exhaustMap — it ignores new search terms while one is loading

questions.explanation: In search you only care about the latest term. switchMap cancels the previous request, avoiding race conditions where a slow older response clobbers a newer one.

options.text: concatMap is mergeMap with a concurrency of 1 — it queues inners and preserves order
They are identical aliases
concatMap cancels previous inners; mergeMap does not
concatMap runs inners in parallel; mergeMap runs them sequentially

questions.explanation: concatMap subscribes to the next inner only after the current one completes — equivalent to mergeMap with concurrency 1 — so emissions stay ordered.

questions.prompt: For a login button, you want to ignore extra clicks while a request is in flight. Which operator fits?

options.text: exhaustMap
switchMap
mergeMap
concatMap

questions.explanation: exhaustMap ignores new outer values while an inner Observable is active — perfect for preventing duplicate submissions from rapid clicks.

questions.prompt: Why is subscribing inside another subscribe (nested subscribe) considered an anti-pattern?

options.text: It loses cancellation, composition, and error propagation and can leak subscriptions
It is a syntax error in RxJS 7
It automatically switches to mergeMap behaviour
It doubles the emission rate

questions.explanation: Nested subscribes break the pipeline: no automatic cancellation of inners, no error propagation, and easy leaks. A flattening operator handles all of that.

questions.prompt: Match each flattening operator to its overlap strategy.

pairs.right: Run all inners concurrently; order not guaranteed
Queue inners; run one at a time, in order
Cancel the previous inner on each new value
Ignore new values while an inner is active

questions.explanation: merge = parallel, concat = sequential, switch = cancel-previous, exhaust = ignore-new. Choosing the right one is a core RxJS skill.
